text.brief: In May 1957 the student Lin Xiling stood before a crowd at Peking University and told them the Party had become a privileged class.
text.record: Mao invited criticism of the Party in the spring of 1957, and intellectuals answered with posters and speeches. On June 8 the People's Daily turned on the critics, and the Anti-Rightist Campaign labeled more than 550,000 people rightists. Many spent two decades in labor camps and internal exile.
text.reading: The invitation mapped the critics before the strike fell, which is Stratagem 13 run on a nation's intellectuals. The Party had fewer honest reporters when the famine came two years later.
text.gapText: Architecture Governance. No rule protected speech the Party itself had invited.
text.fix: Make invited criticism safe by law, because a system that punishes feedback loses its sensors.
